Question B-002-002-001.

Why the correct answer is right: The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) phonetic alphabet gives standard words for letters. That makes a call sign easier to copy through noise or accents.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Use any words which start with the same letters as your call sign for each letter of your call": Any random word may share the first letter, but listeners should not have to decode a private alphabet.
- sourceIndex 2: "Talk louder and faster": Louder and faster speech often makes copy worse; clarity comes from standard spelling and good audio.
- sourceIndex 3: "Turn up your microphone gain": More microphone gain can overdrive audio and still will not identify ambiguous letters.
